To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the synergistic effect of Cu-MOF and reduced graphene oxide in Cu-MOF/graphene nanocomposites results in a promising electrode material for supercapacitive devices.
the Cu-MOF/graphene hybrid composite was successfully synthesized by a hydrothermal method and used as a high-performance electrode material for supercapacitive energy storage devices.

the Cu-MOF/G hybrid composites have been synthesized by an efficient method, and the as-obtained hybrid composites exhibited excellent electrochemical performance, and a high energy density of 34.5 Wh Kg−1 and high power density of 1350 W Kg−1 were achieved.

the synthesis of Cu-MOFs and their hybrid composites with graphene, which are used for supercapacitive applications.
the fabrication of a novel Cu-MOF/G composite as an electrode material for supercapacitance.
the fabrication of Cu-MOF/G hybrid composites with high electrochemical performance for the application of supercapacitor.

Cu-MOFs and graphene nanocomposites are promising electrode materials for high-performance supercapacitors.
the Cu-MOF/G hybrid composites can be a promising candidate for the fabrication of supercapacitors with high energy density and power density.
the prepared Cu-MOF/graphene composite is a promising candidate as electrode material for high-performance supercapacitors.

the Cu-MOF/G hybrid composites have a great potential in energy storage applications.
the Cu-MOF/graphene hybrid nanocomposites could be a promising electrode candidate for the fabrication of high-performance supercapacitors.

the synergistic effects between metal–organic frameworks and graphene can significantly improve electrochemical performance of supercapacitors, which can be extended to other metal–organic frameworks for supercapacitive applications.
